component.name: Helikodu
component.summary: Play and organize your music library, offline

description.p: Helikodu is an audio player and music library manager for your own music, kept on your own computer. It works entirely offline: it never connects to the internet and sends no telemetry.

ul.li: Plays practically every audio format, including the sound track of video files
Gapless playback, bit-perfect output where the hardware allows it, and ReplayGain 2.0 loudness normalization
Choose the sound system, the output device and the mode, or switch them while playing
A library built for large collections, with fast search and play statistics
Media controls, media keys and notifications on GNOME, KDE Plasma and other desktops

description.p: In the Flatpak, Helikodu has no network access at all and asks only for what its features need:

ul.li: Your Music folder, to read and change it: for the library, the tag editor, organizing files and cover files. Other folders are added in the settings
The sound system (PipeWire and PulseAudio), to play and to choose the output device
Reserving a sound card, so that the sound server hands it over for exclusive, bit-perfect output
The login manager (logind), to pause playback before the computer goes to sleep or the screen locks
The system tray, for the optional tray icon

screenshot.caption: Your music library and the player
An album with the details of the selected track
Now Playing with synced lyrics and the signal path
Search the library with a query
Smart playlists made of rules or query text
Choose the sound system, the device and bit-perfect output
A parametric equalizer that reads AutoEQ presets
Edit the tags of several tracks at once
Convert music for phones and other players
Your music library in the dark style

description.p: More sound processing and smarter playback:

ul.li: A compressor with a night mode, room correction by convolution, pitch shift and playback speed
The processing stages in an order of your choice, saved as named chains, and an equalizer for single tracks
Endless play with related tracks, an Auto-DJ, and shuffle that favours or skips tracks
Tracks that sound alike, found on your computer without any online service
Generator playlists, made by steps
Tracks are analysed in the background: crossfades follow the music, silence can be left out or skipped, and a leveller evens out tracks without loudness values
Import play counts, ratings and playlists from Rhythmbox, Strawberry, Clementine, Lollypop and iTunes, and move your own data to another computer
Labels for tracks, albums and artists, and fields of your own
An optional managed music folder
Naming patterns with functions and conditions, and the track table grouped by any field
Music that was playing when Helikodu closed plays on when it starts again
The Flatpak file installs Helikodu from its own signed repository, so that it gets updates
The tray menu in KDE Plasma no longer shows wrong items after it changes
Every page fits a narrow window
Helikodu uses less memory
With Now Playing open, the window can be made as small as elsewhere
The Favourite button shows the same heart on every desktop
The ring around the cover of the playing album is drawn whole

description.p: The release candidate for 1.0: smart playlists and a query language for search, lyrics, a play history, Home and a mini player, tag tools with undo, file organizing, converting and folder sync, a cover manager, a waveform seek bar, library backups, an offline user guide and better screen reader and keyboard access.

The first beta: graphic and parametric equalizers, crossfeed, channel mixing and a limiter, crossfades and fades, loudness measurement, a signal path view, PulseAudio and JACK output, and tracker modules, game music, SID tunes and MIDI files.

The first alpha: a music library with albums, artists, genres, folders, tracks, search and playlists, gapless and bit-perfect playback with ReplayGain, a tag editor, and desktop integration through MPRIS.
